*"Don't you miss having a strong man to lean on?"* Rebecca223 asked, with a hundred-dollar donation. *"Would you give up your business if you met the love of your life?"*

Freya decided to answer.

"A business won't replace a man, and a man won't replace your life's work. Though you don't have to cater to a business the way you do to a lover. And the right business will *always* stay up for you"—here Freya smiled—"which, you have to admit, gives it a distinct advantage over a man."

The chats exploded. The Twitter and Instagram feeds on the side monitors scrolled at a breakneck pace. The feminist community mobilized in full, and the feed suddenly bloomed with colorful-haired avatars like an exotic conservatory. Now it wasn't her assistants but Freya's own fans who were mass-reporting and slinging mud at the right-wing trolls who had swarmed toward the light of her stream from their anonymous loser forums. Right-wingers were always such a hassle.

Still, three hundred and eighty... no, three hundred and ninety thousand live viewers was three hundred and ninety thousand viewers. No matter what they smelled like.

The trolls tried to flood the stream with questions like *"Do you swallow?"* and *"Try shaving your legs"*—zero imagination, just sheer volume. Stupid sad green frogs started popping up in the chat. Freya kept smiling and selectively answering questions, glancing over at her assistants' chat. Like it or not, the comments set the tone. In the end, though, the moderators didn't even need to step in.

The trolls' moms didn't give them more than five dollars for school lunch. So they were utterly crushed by a counterattack from Freya's core audience, who rallied at the call of fan groups across Twitter, TikTok, and Instagram. Rushing to their idol's rescue came stay-at-home moms, nail techs, and small-town college girls. Housewives who had answered the clarion call of the modern economy and traded their soup ladles for oversized smartphones. Plus the men desperate for the attention of all the women above, who had started posing as allies without even noticing they were blowing twenty bucks a month or more on Freya.

Not the most prestigious audience for a serious woman sharing the secrets of *real* success, but a loyal one. And in real business, loyalty counts for a lot.

Right before Freya's eyes, the haters' comments were washed away by twenty- and fifty-dollar messages: *"Go Freya!"* *"Freya, we love you!"* *"#Axelsensexuals!"* The amounts climbed fast, and soon donations under ten dollars weren't even making it onto the screen. At last, she gave a genuine smile.
